Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?
Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?
How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?
How would you explain, step by step, how to find the stationary points of an equation y=f(x)?

In high school, it was my worst subject—endless frustration with equations and proofs that made no sense to me. I barely scraped by with upper secondary level. Way better.","Do you ever get anxious when thinking about mathematics?":"Yes, definitely. Just seeing math symbols sends my heart racing—high school flashbacks of failing tests hit hard. With my neurotic side, even budgeting for cycling gear stresses me out. I get sweaty palms, doubt myself endlessly. Prefer losing myself in novels or classical music to dodge that knot in my stomach. Math anxiety is real for me.","Did you ever use AI to support your math learning in the last year? If yes, how was your experience?":"I tried once last year with ChatGPT for simple interest calculations on a loan—boyfriend suggested it. Stick to apps for basic stuff, not deep math learning.","How would you explain, step by step, how to solve a second order algebraic equation?":"Second order is quadratic: ax² + bx + c = 0. Step 1: Note a, b, c values. Step 2: Calculate discriminant D = b² - 4ac. Step 3: If D ≥ 0, roots are [-b ± √D]/(2a). Positive D: two real roots; zero: one; negative: complex. Still panics me—grab a calculator always!","How would you explain, step by step, how to find the stationary points of an equation y=f(x)?":"Stationary points are where slope is zero, like peaks/valleys. Watch YouTube, don't stress like I do; it's stats magic for big data.","According to you, how can LLMs be used to innovate math learning in schools and universities?":"LLMs rock for math! Unis: simulate proofs, visualize calculus. Integrate with hobbies—math in cooking recipes? Less anxiety, more fun. Open-minded me loves this innovation."},"reasoning_summary":"Answers embody persona's math hatred (hat_subjects), high neuroticism (anxiety admissions), low education (simplistic/vague advanced explanations), high openness/agreeableness (positive AI ideas, helpful tone), casual human voice with personal anecdotes from hobbies/life."}
